referenceName: High-urgency animal emergency service with signal-red wayfinding

source.name: VEG ER for Pets official website
source.sourceType: official direct veterinary-business website, captured in Playwright Chromium
source.rightsEvidence: Requester-attested clearance on 2026-09-29 covers retaining the paired desktop/mobile full-page captures, deriving a design prompt, and using these captures as internal pipeline-model visual references. No source-owner grant was supplied.

referenceDna.annotatedDescription: The emergency-veterinary page prioritizes action through a compact navigation line, a highly visible emergency headline, short urgency context, and a location-entry control. A second image-and-copy chapter establishes scope, followed by four scannable reassurance points, a very large evidence-led metric treatment, explanatory text, review excerpts, an external-coverage wordmark field, an educational article rail, and a black utility footer. The typography is assertive uppercase grotesk with one signal-red accent used for selected words and action labels. Translate the order, speed of scanning, location action, and contrast behavior using verified facts and original assets. Do not reuse the source logo, its numerical claims, testimonials, press marks, photographs, specific red, or branded expression.

heroGeometry.mode: emergency poster paired with a clinic scene and immediate location lookup
heroGeometry.viewport: urgent service and location action are legible in the first screen

navigationGeometry.mode: small wordmark, compressed service links, and a simple mobile menu
navigationGeometry.mobile: menu icon above a vertically stacked emergency headline and finder

typography.scale: short stacked caps, sharp section labels, rare oversized evidence numerals

palette.contrastIntent: emergency actions and essential text remain clear without relying on color alone

imageTreatment.mode: documentary care image with short supporting pet portraits
imageTreatment.crop: rounded rectangular opening image and modular article crops
imageTreatment.focalPoint: show the animal and care context; never put urgent instructions over a busy image

servicePresentation.pattern: problem and care-scope explanation followed by four concise decision principles
servicePresentation.interaction: location finder and optional review/article rails; no required gated interaction

ctaPlacement.early: find-care action appears beside the opening promise

motion.primitive: limited horizontal testimonial or article navigation
motion.library: native CSS or framework primitives; no source scripts
motion.reducedMotion: provide standard previous/next controls and static visible cards

mobileRecomposition.strategy: collapse to emergency headline, locator, image, then short explanatory chapters
rules: keep emergency contact or location action before nonessential content
stack the four decision principles instead of shrinking them
use clipped rails only with visible controls and keyboard access
avoid tiny trust marks and dense legal text in the primary reading path

prohibitedPatterns: copying the source wordmark, exact red treatment, photographs, reviews, press logos, statistics, copy, or claims
using emergency or 24-hour availability unless client facts confirm it
fake medical authority or urgency language
using external ratings as invented proof
decorative counters that imply business results

requiredSignatureElements.description: A short, visually forceful problem-led opening puts an appropriate location or contact action close to the headline.
A compact set of distinct care or process principles is arranged for fast scanning, not as repeated generic cards.
A small education or FAQ chapter helps visitors understand a next step after the urgent opening.

acceptanceChecks: Urgency is explicit only when the client's verified service and availability support it.
Location or contact is a functional action, not a decorative search field.
Large numbers are omitted unless the client provides a source and date.
Mobile makes the primary action reachable without horizontal scrolling or overlay obstruction.
No source copy, logo, photo, review, rating, press mark, numerical claim, or exact brand palette is reused.

review.notes: Official page returned HTTP 200 at both viewports. Full-page screenshots were inspected with the cookie notice dismissed in the temporary browser profile. Source scripts reported errors and several empty image references that resolved to the site root; the core emergency imagery and sections render. These source defects are not transferred as design guidance.
